/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j

/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2

/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)

/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
  LinearMap.pi
    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)

/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)

/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
the two overlap restrictions. -/
lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]

/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

/-! ### The certificate -/

/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
  flat_coker_diff :
    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))

end DivisorAdaptation

/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/

variable (n : ℕ)

/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
adaptation. -/
structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n

/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)

namespace DivFam

variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]

/-- The class of a certified family. -/
def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F

10	# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause
13	
14	`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`
15	
16	(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
17	`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
18	(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
19	
20	The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
21	inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
22	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
23	support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.
24	
25	This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
26	locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
27	too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:
28	
29	* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
30	* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
31	  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.
32	
33	The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
34	subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
35	for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
36	image.
37	
38	## Main declarations
39	
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
41	  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
42	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
43	  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
44	-/

81	    Module.Projective R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
82	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
83	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=

name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

namespace Scheme.LocalEquations

variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)

/-- **The leak locus of a support trace**: the part of the closure of
`supportLocus ∩ U` that escapes `U`.  The trace `supportLocus ∩ U` is closed in `X`
iff the leak locus is empty (`isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`);
its base image under a universally closed structure morphism is closed
(`isClosed_image_supportLeak`), so the trace is closed over the complementary base
open — the Zariski-local piece-isolation mechanism of the DDR-4 finiteness input. -/
def supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : Set X :=
  closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) \ (U : Set X)

lemma isClosed_supportLeak (U : X.Opens) : IsClosed (d.supportLeak U) :=
  isClosed_closure.sdiff U.isOpen

/-- The leak locus lies in the support outside the open: leaks are support points. -/
lemma supportLeak_subset_sdiff (U : X.Opens) :
    d.supportLeak U ⊆ d.supportLocus \ (U : Set X) := fun _ hx =>
  ⟨closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx.1, hx.2⟩

/-- The support trace on an open is closed in the whole space iff nothing leaks. -/
lemma isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens) :
    IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) ↔ d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    rw [supportLeak, h.closure_eq, Set.sdiff_eq_empty]
    exact Set.inter_subset_right
  · intro h
    rw [supportLeak, Set.sdiff_eq_empty] at h
    exact isClosed_of_closure_subset fun x hx =>
      ⟨closure_minimal Set.inter_subset_left d.isClosed_supportLocus hx, h hx⟩

/-- **The fibre no-leak criterion** — the named threading slot for the fibrewise data
of the (c1)-finite clause: if over every base point the fibre of the closure of the
trace stays inside `U`, the leak locus is empty.  In the CertUniv instantiation the
hypothesis is produced from the seed design and the P-fib-N fibre analysis (the fibre
support is a finite set of pairwise-incomparable closed points, each isolated inside
its piece). -/
lemma supportLeak_eq_empty_of_forall_fibre (f : X ⟶ S) {U : X.Opens}
    (hfib : ∀ s : S, f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X))
      ⊆ (U : Set X)) :
    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
  rintro x ⟨hxc, hxU⟩
  exact hxU (hfib (f.base x) ⟨rfl, hxc⟩)

/-- **The base image of the leak locus is closed** under a universally closed morphism
(the properness licence): its complement is the Zariski-open locus of the base over
which the support trace on `U` is closed — the tube-side mechanism for producing the
closed-trace input Zariski-locally on the base. -/
theorem isClosed_image_supportLeak (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] (U : X.Opens) :
    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLeak U) :=
  f.isClosedMap _ (d.isClosed_supportLeak U)

end Scheme.LocalEquations

10	# The certificate of a support-separated adaptation
11	
12	The DD-R certificate lane was built around the equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ_left − δ_right)`
13	of the two overlap-restriction arrows.  Its two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4), and the
14	kernel-spanning input of `isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`, are the genuinely hard
15	relative content — `DivSchemeHighWindowSyzygy.lean` shows the kernel-spanning law is
16	*equivalent* to the flatness one is trying to prove, so no cleverer submodule evades it.
17	
18	This file records the escape hatch that the *pointwise* gate opens up.  Because
19	`isLocallyCertified_of_forall_prime_exists_certified_adaptation` accepts **any**
20	adaptation over the shrunken base, we are free to choose one whose pieces are
21	**support-separated**: each off-diagonal overlap misses the divisor, so its overlap
22	colength vanishes.  For such an adaptation
23	
24	* `δ_left = δ_right` on the nose (`deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated`), hence
25	* `W(d)` is the whole product `∏_j colength j` (`gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'`), and
26	* both cokernels are *zero* modules, so (c3)/(c4) hold for free
27	  (`flat_coker_incl_of_separated`, `flat_coker_diff_of_separated`).
28	
29	What remains of the certificate is only the (c1) data — chart-local colengths finite
30	projective — plus the constant-rank reading of their product.  Both are already available:
31	(c1) from the support tube (`SupportTubeFinite.lean`, `SupportTube.lean`) and the rank as a
32	sum of the per-piece ranks (`Module.rankAtStalk_pi`).
33	
34	This is a genuine reduction, not a repackaging: the hypothesis it trades for is the
35	*geometric separation* of the chosen pieces, which the tube produces one base point at a
36	time, whereas the discharged hypotheses were fibrewise flatness statements over a
37	nonreduced base.
38

41	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule_eq_top_of_separated'` — the equalizer
42	  collapses over an arbitrary base ring (the field-level lemma generalized).
43	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.deltaLeft_eq_deltaRight_of_separated` — the Čech
44	  difference vanishes.
45	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation.isCertified_of_separated` — the certificate from
46	  (c1) plus a rank reading, with no kernel-spanning and no flatness input.

  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)

/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
the two overlap restrictions. -/
lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]

/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule

/-! ### The certificate -/

/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
  flat_coker_diff :
    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))

end DivisorAdaptation

/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/

variable (n : ℕ)

/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
adaptation. -/
structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n

/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
  iseqv :=
    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩

/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)

namespace DivFam

variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]

/-- The class of a certified family. -/
def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F

body: 'THE Z-CLOPEN CERTIFICATE PRINCIPLE (DD-1/DD-2 lanes, 2026-07-17 — three independent
  sightings in one day; treat as a standing design constraint for every DAT-D brick).


  A DivisorAdaptation piece carries an R-finite-projective colength — clause (c1)
  of IsCertified — IFF the piece''s trace on the divisor scheme Z = V(D) (finite flat
  over Spec R) is CLOPEN in Z. Any construction that slices Z along the base (basic-open
  refinement of pieces, denominator-cleared pieces from a localization cover, Z-blind
  extraction) produces section rings like R_u that are NOT finite over R, and the
  certificate is unrecoverable — the localization-span descent lemmas'' hypotheses
  are FALSE, not merely hard. Canonical counterexample: R = k[u], zero-section divisor,
  cleared piece D(u-tilde): colength = R_u.


  Consequences adjudicated today: (1) the DD-1 pt-transport seam could NOT be fixed
  by extraction + certificate transport (certificates are not refinement-stable) —
  fixed instead by the S1 carrier surgery (point-free eqn_rel, total mapAlg, commit
  19c79359); (2) DD-2 S5''s glued adaptation could NOT take its certificate from denominator-cleared
  pieces (spec-dd-2 section-5 route corrected in the addendum) — the gluing keystone
  landed CONDITIONAL on hcert (exists_glue_of_away_compat_of_certifiedRep, commit
  1758fad90).


  THE MISSING BRICK (next in the DD-2 lane; coordinate with DD-R before speccing —
  same substrate as DDR-4''s engine bridge, spec-dd-r section-7 risk 1): W-as-algebra
  extraction — the glued colength W(d) of a certified family is a finite projective
  R-ALGEBRA (= Gamma(Z)); its canonical idempotents (glued via the module-localization
  sheaf sequence over the away cover) split Z into packets; CRT-separated chart generators
  give packet-swallowing basic-open pieces whose traces are clopen; that adaptation
  carries the certificate and discharges hcert, upgrading the conditional keystone
  to the pinned DivFam.exists_glue_of_away_compat. Only then can S6 deliver divFunctor
  at full strength for DDR-9.'

10	# No-leak over a shrunken base, with no fibre hypothesis
11	
12	The certificate assemblers consume, per piece `j`, the fibrewise clause
13	
14	`∀ s, (fibre over s) ∩ closure (supp ∩ pieces j) ⊆ pieces j`
15	
16	(`isCertified_of_noLeak_kernel_spanning`), equivalently emptiness of the **leak locus**
17	`supportLeak (pieces j) = closure (supp ∩ pieces j) \ pieces j`
18	(`Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty`).
19	
20	The `tube-fibre` leaf of the DD-R lane tried to obtain this by putting the whole support
21	inside a single piece.  That shape is refuted — `DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`,
22	`not_exists_unique_support_piece`: both pinned charts carry a partition of unity, so a
23	support point of `V₀ ⊓ V₁` always lies in two distinct pieces.
24	
25	This file gets the clause a different way, and **without any fibre analysis**.  The leak
26	locus is closed, and under a universally closed structure morphism its base image is closed
27	too (`isClosed_image_supportLeak`).  So:
28	
29	* over the *open complement* of that base image, nothing leaks;
30	* that complement is a Zariski neighbourhood of every base point it contains, refinable to a
31	  basic open — the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise gate consumes.
32	
33	The leak locus is a genuine obstruction only over its own base image, which is a **closed**
34	subset of `Spec R`. So the no-leak clause is available on a Zariski-dense open of the base
35	for free; what a fibre analysis is still needed for is the base points *inside* that closed
36	image.
37	
38	## Main declarations
39	
40	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty` — a basic
41	  open around any base point outside the leak's image, over which nothing leaks.
42	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty` —
43	  leak-freeness over an open of the base gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.
44	-/

58	/-! ## The idempotent brick
59	
60	I-0209 predicted the shape of the missing construction: the canonical idempotents of a
61	finite projective colength algebra split the divisor scheme into packets, and a piece
62	swallowing a packet has a clopen trace, hence carries the certificate.  The algebraic core
63	of that is elementary and is recorded here: cutting by an idempotent produces a **direct
64	summand**, so projectivity is inherited with no flatness or finiteness input. -/
65	
66	section Idempotent
67	
68	variable {R B : Type u} [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
69	
70	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
71	-- The `Ideal`-to-`Submodule` coercion in the quotient makes `liftQ` elaboration expensive.
72	/-- **Cutting by an idempotent gives a direct summand.** For `e` idempotent, multiplication
73	by `e` is a well-defined `R`-linear section of `B ↠ B ⧸ (1 - e)`, so the quotient is a
74	retract of `B` and inherits projectivity.
75	
76	This is the algebraic core of the packet-splitting construction I-0209 asks for: an
77	idempotent of the colength algebra cuts out a clopen packet, and the corresponding quotient
78	is projective for free. -/
79	theorem Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem
80	    [Module.Projective R B] (e : B) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
81	    Module.Projective R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
82	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
83	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=
84	    P.liftQ (LinearMap.mulLeft R e) (by
85	      intro x hx
86	      have hx' : x ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e} := hx
87	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hx'
88	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hx'
89	      change e * ((1 - e) * c) = 0
90	      rw [← mul_assoc, mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self, zero_mul]) with hs
91	  refine Module.Projective.of_split s P.mkQ (LinearMap.ext fun y => ?_)
92	  obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := P.mkQ_surjective y
93	  change P.mkQ (e * b) = P.mkQ b
94	  rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
95	  change e * b - b ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e}
96	  rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
97	  exact ⟨-b, by ring⟩
98	
99	set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
100	-- Same elaboration cost as the projective companion.
101	/-- **The flat companion.** A retract of a flat module is flat, so an idempotent cut also
102	inherits flatness.  This is the form that applies to the DD-R pieces: the piece section
103	rings `Γ(relCurve C R, pieces j)` are known **flat** over `R` (localizations of the free
104	pinned-chart rings, `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces`) rather than projective, so it is
105	this version that discharges the (c1) input from a packet idempotent. -/
106	theorem Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_one_sub_of_isIdempotentElem
107	    [Module.Flat R B] (e : B) (he : IsIdempotentElem e) :
108	    Module.Flat R (B ⧸ (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R) := by
109	  set P := (Ideal.span {1 - e}).restrictScalars R with hP
110	  set s : (B ⧸ P) →ₗ[R] B :=
111	    P.liftQ (LinearMap.mulLeft R e) (by
112	      intro x hx
113	      have hx' : x ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e} := hx
114	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at hx'
115	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := hx'
116	      change e * ((1 - e) * c) = 0
117	      rw [← mul_assoc, mul_sub, mul_one, he.eq, sub_self, zero_mul]) with hs
118	  exact Module.Flat.of_retract s P.mkQ (LinearMap.ext fun y => by
119	    obtain ⟨b, rfl⟩ := P.mkQ_surjective y
120	    change P.mkQ (e * b) = P.mkQ b
121	    rw [← sub_eq_zero, ← map_sub, Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
122	    change e * b - b ∈ Ideal.span {1 - e}
123	    rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton]
124	    exact ⟨-b, by ring⟩)

126	end Idempotent

130	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (d : X.LocalEquations)
131	
132	/-- **A leak-free basic open around any base point outside the leak's image.** The leak
133	locus is closed and its base image is closed under a universally closed morphism, so the
134	complement is open; refining it to a basic open (`PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens`)
135	gives the `Localization.Away` shape the pointwise certificate gate consumes. -/
136	theorem exists_basicOpen_supportLeak_eq_empty (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R))
137	    [UniversallyClosed f] (U : X.Opens) {p : PrimeSpectrum R}
138	    (hp : (p : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) ∉ f.base '' d.supportLeak U) :
139	    ∃ r : R, r ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
140	      f.base ⁻¹' (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : Set (PrimeSpectrum R))
141	        ∩ d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
142	  classical
143	  have hopen : IsOpen ((f.base '' d.supportLeak U)ᶜ) :=
144	    (d.isClosed_image_supportLeak f U).isOpen_compl
145	  obtain ⟨W, hWmem, hpW, hWsub⟩ :=
146	    PrimeSpectrum.isTopologicalBasis_basic_opens.exists_subset_of_mem_open
147	      (a := p) hp hopen
148	  obtain ⟨r, rfl⟩ := hWmem
149	  refine ⟨r, (PrimeSpectrum.mem_basicOpen r p).mp hpW, ?_⟩
150	  rw [Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem]
151	  rintro x ⟨hxb, hxl⟩
152	  exact hWsub hxb ⟨x, hxl, rfl⟩
153	
154	/-- **Leak-freeness over a base open gives the assembler's fibrewise clause there.** If no
155	point over the base set `V` leaks out of `U`, then for every base point `s ∈ V` the fibre of
156	the closure of the *restricted* trace stays in `U`.
157	
158	This is the bridge from the closed-image mechanism to the shape
159	`finite_colength_of_forall_fibre_closure_subset` consumes: the closure is taken of the trace
160	restricted over `V`, which only shrinks it, so a leak would have to be a leak of the
161	unrestricted trace. -/
162	theorem forall_fibre_closure_subset_of_supportLeak_inter_eq_empty
163	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) (U : X.Opens) {V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R))}
164	    (hV : f.base ⁻¹' V ∩ d.supportLeak U = ∅) :
165	    ∀ s ∈ V, f.base ⁻¹' {s}
166	        ∩ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X) ∩ f.base ⁻¹' V)
167	      ⊆ (U : Set X) := by
168	  intro s hs x hx
169	  by_contra hxU
170	  -- `x` is in the closure of the full trace, and outside `U`, hence a leak
171	  have hcl : x ∈ closure (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) :=
172	    closure_mono Set.inter_subset_left hx.2
173	  have hxV : x ∈ f.base ⁻¹' V := by
174	    have : f.base x = s := hx.1
175	    rw [Set.mem_preimage, this]; exact hs
176	  exact Set.eq_empty_iff_forall_notMem.mp hV x ⟨hxV, hcl, hxU⟩
177	
178	/-! ## No-leak IS the Z-clopen condition
179	
180	The recorded design constraint of this project (memory I-0209, "the Z-clopen certificate
181	principle") says a piece carries an `R`-finite colength exactly when its trace on the divisor
182	scheme is *clopen* in that scheme.  The following two lemmas identify that principle with the
183	leak locus, so the two vocabularies are the same statement:
184	
185	the piece trace `supp ∩ U` is always **open** in the subspace `supp` (as `U` is open), so it
186	is clopen there precisely when it is closed in the ambient space — precisely when nothing
187	leaks. -/
188	
189	/-- **Leak-freeness is clopen-ness of the trace in the support.** The forward direction of
190	the identification with the Z-clopen principle (I-0209). -/
191	theorem isClopen_trace_of_supportLeak_eq_empty (U : X.Opens)
192	    (h : d.supportLeak U = ∅) :
193	    IsClopen ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)) := by
194	  have hclosed : IsClosed (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) :=
195	    (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mpr h
196	  refine ⟨?_, U.isOpen.preimage continuous_subtype_val⟩
197	  have heq : (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X)
198	      = (fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X)) := by
199	    ext x; simp
200	  rw [heq]
201	  exact hclosed.preimage continuous_subtype_val
202	
203	/-- The converse: a clopen trace leaks nothing.  Together with the previous lemma, the
204	assembler's per-piece no-leak clause and the Z-clopen principle of I-0209 are literally the
205	same condition — so the certificate lane's finiteness obligation was never about fibres, it
206	was about the trace being a connected-component-like piece of the divisor scheme. -/
207	theorem supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace (U : X.Opens)
208	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹' (U : Set X))) :
209	    d.supportLeak U = ∅ := by
210	  refine (d.isClosed_supportLocus_inter_iff_supportLeak_eq_empty U).mp ?_
211	  -- a set closed in the closed subspace `supp` is closed in `X`
212	  obtain ⟨T, hT, hTeq⟩ := (isClosed_induced_iff (f := fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val)).mp h
213	  have heq : d.supportLocus ∩ (U : Set X) = d.supportLocus ∩ T := by
214	    ext x
215	    constructor
216	    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxU⟩
217	      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mpr hxU⟩
218	    · rintro ⟨hxs, hxT⟩
219	      exact ⟨hxs, (Set.ext_iff.mp hTeq ⟨x, hxs⟩).mp hxT⟩
220	  rw [heq]
221	  exact d.isClosed_supportLocus.inter hT
222	
223	end Scheme.LocalEquations

225	/-! ## The (c1) clause from a clopen trace
226	
227	Assembling the identification with the landed finiteness engine: a clopen piece trace gives
228	the assembler's `hnoLeak` at that piece, hence its `Module.Finite` colength.  Combined with
229	`SupportTube.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` this is the whole (c1) input,
230	so under the Z-clopen hypothesis the certificate's finiteness side needs no fibre analysis.
231	
232	What remains outstanding for the lane is only the *production* of the clopen trace, i.e.
233	I-0209's `W`-as-algebra extraction. `PrimeSpectrum.isClopen_iff_zeroLocus` and
234	`PrimeSpectrum.exists_idempotent_basicOpen_eq_of_isClopen` are the mathlib translations that
235	turn a clopen packet of the divisor scheme into the idempotent the brick above consumes. -/
236	
237	section Clopen
238	
239	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} [IsProper C.hom]
240	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
241	variable {pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite pi]
242	variable {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
243	
244	namespace DivisorAdaptation
245	
246	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R pi d)
247	
248	/-- **A clopen piece trace gives the (c1)-finite clause at that piece.** Reading the
249	identification `supportLeak = ∅ ↔ clopen trace` into the landed finiteness engine
250	`finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty`. -/
251	theorem finite_colength_of_isClopen_trace (j : A.index)
252	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹'
253	      (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R)))) :
254	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) :=
255	  A.finite_colength_of_supportLeak_eq_empty j
256	    (d.supportLeak_eq_empty_of_isClopen_trace _ h)
257	
258	/-- **The full (c1) data at a piece with clopen trace.** Finiteness from the clopen trace,
259	projectivity from fibrewise regularity of the piece equation — which for a seed adaptation
260	is landed (`ThetaGeneratorSeed.divisorAdaptation_fibre_regular`).  No fibre containment and
261	no flatness of a Čech cokernel enters. -/
262	theorem finite_and_projective_colength_of_isClopen_trace [IsNoetherianRing R] (j : A.index)
263	    (h : IsClosed ((fun x : d.supportLocus => x.val) ⁻¹'
264	      (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))))
265	    (hreg : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
266	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
267	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
268	        nonZeroDivisors
269	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
270	    Module.Finite R (A.colength j) ∧ Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := by
271	  haveI := A.finite_colength_of_isClopen_trace j h
272	  exact ⟨‹_›, A.projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField j hreg⟩
